sections.html:
• Name: Matano Crab (also Blue Matano Crab, Blue Crab)
  • Scientific name: Syntripsa matannensis
  • Type: fully aquatic crab
  • Minimum tank size: about 90 litres
  • Breeding: very difficult
  • Carapace size: 3–6 cm
  • Leg span: 7–12 cm
  • KH: 4–8 (3–10)
  • TDS: 100 (50–150)
  • Nitrate: less than 20 ppm
  • Diet: omnivore / carnivore
  • Temperament: aggressive / territorial
  • Life span: up to 3 years
  • Colour: purple-blue

Choose healthy, active crabs with intact limbs and normal bright colour, from a reputable store. Purchase size is usually 2.5–5 cm. If keeping multiple crabs, a good ratio is one male to 1–2 females, which can reduce aggression.

The Matano crab is known from a number of localities around Lake Matano in South Sulawesi, Indonesia, where it appears to be evenly distributed throughout the lake and lives alongside other freshwater crabs such as the Panther crab (Parathelphusa pantherina). The name 'Matano' comes from the lake, which is of tectonic origin, which accounts for its extraordinary depth.

Taxonomy: Kingdom Animalia, Phylum Arthropoda, Subphylum Crustacea, Class Malacostraca, Order Decapoda, Family Gecarcinucidae, Genus Syntripsa.

This species is mainly found on the sandy and rocky floors of Lake Matano, which has a surface area of about 164 km². During the day the crab can be seen wandering and feeding on snails and other organic matter on the open lake floor.

Endemic crabs in Lake Matano are found more in the southern part of the lake than in the northern part, because the southern waters are not steep and have a sandy bottom.

The species is listed as endangered by the IUCN Red List because its habitat is declining due to pollution from nickel mining on the lake shores, habitat destruction and non-native species. Harvesting, including gravid females, by local people for food or for the aquarium trade, and commercial fishing are major threats.

At least a 90-litre tank is needed for Matano crabs; a 40-litre tank is not enough. It is best to get the biggest aquarium that fits the available space, so the crabs are not cramped as they grow and there is room for tankmates.

Matano crabs are excellent climbers, escape artists and active scavengers.

Before adding Matano crabs, the aquarium should be well cycled and properly matured. Ideally use RO/DI water with GH/KH+ remineralisers.

They like warm water of 26–30°C and a higher pH of 7.8–8.2. Use a thermometer to monitor the water temperature; a heater may be needed if the aquarium is in a cool place.

Like all invertebrates they need careful acclimation.

To replicate the conditions of Lake Matano and control water quality, use RO/DI water and remineralisers (Salty Shrimp Sulawesi Mineral 8.5 and Salty Shrimp Mineral 7.5).

Provide an air pump or a strong filter outlet to promote aeration. A sandy substrate is preferable; to mimic the natural habitat, some gravel or small rocks can be added. Keep most openings sealed, as the crabs climb out given the chance.

Feed a well-balanced crab diet for complete nutrition and good growth. Matano crabs are omnivorous scavengers and not picky: they eat everything from dead fish to decaying organic matter, as well as frozen food, bloodworms and calcium supplements to help maintain shell health. Do not overfeed.

To improve colouration, products such as Hikari Tropical Crab Cuisine, which contain astaxanthin, can be given.

Feed once a day or every two days and remove uneaten food after 24 hours to prevent foul smell and mould. Always thaw frozen food properly before feeding.

Avoid any medication containing a lot of copper, as copper is deadly to invertebrates.

Matano crabs are a little aggressive, especially around small fish and snails. They are nocturnal. Males in particular are territorial and will not tolerate their own species. They are great climbers.

Suitable tankmates are fast-moving fish such as tetras, guppies, mollies, catfish and other tropical fish, though the crab may occasionally catch one. The same applies to dwarf shrimp, such as cardinal shrimp. Keeping them with snails is a bad idea. Although in the wild they share the lake with Panther crabs, keeping the two together is not advised, as they will fight.

Molting: like other crustaceans, they shed their exoskeleton as they grow. A fully grown crab molts about every 8 weeks. During this time the crab is less active and associates less with tankmates. Do not touch it, as it is very vulnerable and may die if disturbed. After molting it eats its old exoskeleton for nutrients. Calcium is needed to harden the new shell.
At the same age, males are relatively larger than females and have bigger claws.

Description: bright purple colouration; large purple square carapace; ambulatory legs of normal length, the second pair the largest; large powerful chelae (unequal); white joints and eyestalks; inflated branchial regions; shallow cervical groove; T-shaped abdomen. Carapace width averages 3–6 cm and leg span reaches 7–12 cm. Matano crabs are fully aquatic but can leave the water, so the aquarium must be secured against escape. They can live up to 3 years.

They are good scavengers and help keep the substrate clean, but their aggressive nature limits options in a community tank.
